newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi pays second tranche of contractors bonds.
newsitem.headline: Saudi pays second tranche of contractors bonds.

text.p: Saudi Arabia has made more progress in meeting arrears to contractors with the redemption of a second tranche of special contractor bonds, bankers said on Tuesday.
They said they received payments for bonds which matured on Monday. "Payments came through yesterday (Monday). There was no problem," one banker said.
Saudi Arabia had in March 1995 issued special bonds estimated to be worth 3.75 billion riyals ($1.0 billion) to make a dent in the estimated $5 billion outstanding to contractors.

Bankers said the bonds which matured on Monday represented a third of that issue. The first tranche matured in March 1996. In April 1996 it issued more bonds estimated to be worth five to six billion riyals.
Some contractors had cashed in their bonds at banks before maturity at a discount.

The debt had been mounting since the early 1990s when the kingdom fell behind on payments to contractors, suppliers and farmers as a result of huge Gulf War liabilities and soft world oil prices. Some have been waiting for years.
